title: Touring with Beasley Smith
summary: After Winegard he rehearsed with other bands then joined Beasley Smith's Nashville travelling band, touring New England and the upper South until Smith's eyesight failed.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Okay. Then after Frank Weinagar Weingard, it says here you left New York with Beasley Smith. Is that right, was that next?

Well, more or less. There was probably a little -- let's see, I rehearsed and played a few things with, oh, a band by the name of Houston Ray and Will Osborne, and but then I joined Beasley. Beasley was a travelling band. He was out of Nashville, Tennessee, and I joined his band and we toured around all over New England and Pennsylvania and parts of the south. Not the deep south. Virginia and North Carolina and Tennessee.
How big was the Beasley Smith band?

It was the same thing there. We had the three brass, two trumpets, trombone and three saxophones, and of course Beasley was the piano player, and the guitar, bass and drums. That was the standard instrumentation in those days.
And so that would have been about what year?

Well, let's see, that would be after Frank Weinagar Weingard, and I guess that would be around 1930, maybe into '31. And following -- well, we broke up. Beasley started to lose his eyesight and he had to disband the band. Fortunately he didn't lose it. They were able to rectify it. But -- and
